description: An XY display, named ETCHASKETCHOSCOPE on the panel. One voltage moves a drawn beam horizontally and another moves it vertically, and the trace fades away over a settable time

params.text: How far a given voltage moves the beam left and right
Shifts the whole trace left and right
How far a given voltage moves the beam up and down
Shifts the whole trace up and down
How long the trace takes to fade, in seconds
The width of the drawn beam, in pixels
Scales the CV modulating the horizontal scale
Scales the CV modulating the horizontal offset
Scales the CV modulating the vertical scale
Scales the CV modulating the vertical offset
Scales the CV modulating the beam width
The longest straight segment drawn from one sample to the next, in pixels

inputs.text: The voltage that moves the beam left and right, marked X
The voltage that moves the beam up and down, marked Y
A CV modulating the horizontal scale
A CV modulating the vertical scale
A CV modulating the horizontal offset
A CV modulating the vertical offset
A CV modulating the beam width

notes: three inputs take 0-10V each to set the red, green and blue of the beam, and are read only while all three have cables in them
menu: Show Axis — draws the axes across the display
Show Grid — draws a grid across the display
History Fades Exponentially — the older part of the trace fades away exponentially
Faster And Less Resolution — draws at a lower resolution for less processor time, with Show Vectors joining the samples by lines and Show Points drawing them as separate points
Use Beam Size CV IN as Z channel — keeps the beam size voltage for each sample, so it varies along the trace rather than setting one width for all of it
Burn-in Luminosity — sets the brightness of the burn-in the trace leaves behind
Blue Beam — draws the trace in blue, with Green Beam and White Beam as the other two colours
